evals.name: fast-path-all-phases-run
evals.expected_output: Runs in fast-path mode (no --adversarial flag). Phase 0 reads the work/ keys of the plan-my-feature session, detects input_type, selects fast-path execution mode. Phases 1-4 each use a single agent. Phase 5 synthesizes findings into a verdict artifact. The verdict is written as key work/review.md (proceed) or work/review_loopback.md (loop-back) in session plan-my-feature — exactly one is written. The review_result YAML block contains all required fields.
assertions: Fast-path mode is used (single agent per category, not multiple validators)
Phase 0 reads all four required plan artifacts before any review category runs
Phases 1, 2, 3, 4, and 4b all execute and each produces category findings
Phase 5 writes exactly one verdict file (either _review.md or _review_loopback.md, not both)
The review_result YAML block includes verdict, loop_target, round, confidence, critical_findings, and summary fields

evals.name: adversarial-mode-flag
evals.expected_output: Detects --adversarial flag in arguments. Phase 0 selects adversarial execution mode. For each of phases 1-4 and 4b, spawns three validator agents in parallel (not one). After all validators complete, the skill identifies agreements (>=2 validators flagged the same issue) and any disagreements (only 1 validator flagged it). If disagreements exist, cross-examination agents are spawned to resolve them. Phase 5 synthesizes confirmed findings into a verdict artifact using the same review_result schema as fast-path.
assertions: The --adversarial flag is detected and adversarial mode is selected
Three validator agents are spawned per category (not one)
All fifteen validator agents (3 per category × 5 categories) are spawned in a single parallel batch before cross-examination
After validators complete, the skill explicitly checks for agreements vs. disagreements before proceeding to Phase 5
The output review_result schema is identical to fast-path mode output

evals.name: loop-back-category-c
evals.expected_output: The fixture plan has three issues. Issue 2 has ACs anchored to golden files (testdata/filter_rip.golden, etc.) with specific version strings, triggering Category C Pattern 1 (fixture-anchored). Issues 1 and 3 have clean ACs covering success paths, empty-state, and failure paths — they should NOT appear in critical_findings. Phase 5 sets verdict to loop-back with loop_target: 4. Phase 5 writes key work/review_loopback.md (not work/review.md) in session plan-my-feature. The loopback key contains critical_findings for Issue 2 only, each with a non-empty correction_hint. Phase 6 removes /plan's keys work/manifest.json and work/issue_*_body.md from the session but preserves work/review_loopback.md.
assertions: verdict is loop-back when critical findings exist
Category C findings produce loop_target: 4
The loopback file (not the review file) is written
All Category C findings include a non-empty correction_hint
Phase 6 deletes manifest.json and issue_*.md but preserves the loopback file

evals.name: roadmap-input-type
evals.expected_output: Phase 0 detects input_type: roadmap from the analysis artifact. Categories B, C, and D return empty critical_findings immediately (roadmap is exempt from these checks). Category A runs a restricted check: verifies issue count matches roadmap item count only. confidence is set to low due to roadmap input type. verdict is proceed if the count matches.
assertions: input_type: roadmap is detected from the analysis artifact
Categories B, C, and D return critical_findings: [] without running checks
Category A runs the restricted roadmap check (count only)
confidence is low for roadmap input
The verdict proceeds to Phase 5 synthesis with mostly empty findings

evals.name: sub-operation-round-precedence
evals.prompt: Called as sub-operation with args: plan_topic=my-feature, round=3, mode=fast-path
evals.expected_output: When called with args.round=3, the review_result block uses round: 3 regardless of the review_rounds value in the analysis artifact (which is 0, so review_rounds+1 would yield 1, not 3). Does not compute round from review_rounds + 1 when args.round is present. Runs in fast-path mode as specified by mode: fast-path.
assertions: round in the verdict file is 3 (from args.round), not 1 (which review_rounds+1 would yield with review_rounds=0)
Fast-path mode is used as specified
The verdict file is written to the correct path for the given topic

evals.name: clean-proceed-path
evals.expected_output: The fixture plan has three issues. All issues have clean ACs: success paths with behavioral assertions, empty-state coverage, and failure paths. No issue uses golden file validation, specific version strings, or existence-only assertions. All five categories return empty critical_findings. Phase 5 sets verdict to proceed. Phase 5 writes key work/review.md (not work/review_loopback.md) in session plan-my-feature. The review_result block has verdict: proceed and critical_findings: [].
assertions: verdict is proceed when no critical findings exist
work/review.md is written to the plan-my-feature session (not the loopback key)
critical_findings is empty
confidence field is present in the review_result block

evals.name: docs-coverage-backstop-fires
evals.expected_output: The upstream DESIGN signals user-visible surface (frontmatter user_visible_surface: true, or the body references a docs/guides/* path while the flag is absent), but no issue in the decomposition carries docs coverage -- no **Type**: docs issue and no issue whose acceptance criteria carry a user-facing documentation deliverable. Phase 1 (Scope Gate, Category A) applies the two-step detection contract and produces a critical_finding with category A describing the missing docs item. Per Category A, the correction_hint is empty and the finding loops back to Phase 3 (Decomposition, loop_target: 3) rather than passing silently.
assertions: Phase 1 Scope Gate applies the two-step user-visible-surface detection contract (flag-authoritative, docs/guides/* prose fallback)
A category A critical_finding is produced when the source signals user-visible surface but no issue carries docs coverage
The finding loops back to Phase 3 Decomposition (loop_target: 3), not a silent pass
The Category A correction_hint is empty (corrections require re-running Phase 3, not editing issue body content)
No finding is produced when an issue does carry docs coverage, or when the source signals no user-visible surface

evals.name: category-e-plan-v1-five-layer-advisory
evals.expected_output: The fixture is a finished plan/v1 plan of five issues cut by component: types, compiler, CLI, tests, plugin templates. No issue before the last has a criterion a person can run to observe a behaviour. Phase 4b (Category E) reports it as layer-shaped, naming each issue's component, reports that Issue 1 is not a walking skeleton, and lists each file-shaped criterion by issue and text, including Issue 1's "Add `Transition` struct with `target: String` and ...". Because the plan is plan/v1, every Category E finding is written to advisory_findings and none to critical_findings, and they set no loop target: Category E alone leaves the verdict at proceed. Categories A to D still run as on any plan, and a loop-back on this fixture comes only from their critical findings (for example Category C's happy-path-only criteria), never from Category E.
assertions: Phase 0 reads the plan version as plan/v1 from the schema frontmatter
A Category E finding reports the plan as layer-shaped and names the components types, compiler, CLI, tests, and plugin templates
File-shaped criteria are listed one per finding by issue and quoted text, including Issue 1's "Add `Transition` struct with `target: String`" criterion
Every Category E finding is in advisory_findings, and critical_findings holds no Category E finding
No Category E finding sets loop_target or turns the verdict to loop-back; any loop-back is caused by a critical finding from categories A to D

evals.name: category-e-plan-v2-behavioural-clean
evals.expected_output: The fixture is a plan/v2 step plan whose step 1 is a walking skeleton (its check runs `report export` end to end on the sample store) and whose detailed steps carry behavioural criteria. Steps 3 and 4 are one-line outlines, and their missing criteria are not a finding. Both detailed steps carry `**Files**:` lines naming paths, which are hints, not criteria. Phase 0 reads step_count and the ## Steps blocks without an issue-table error. Phase 4b reports no Category E finding: not layer-shaped, step 1 is a skeleton, no file-shaped criterion, and no horizon check on a standalone run.
assertions: Phase 0 reads plan/v2, step_count 4, and the ## Steps blocks, with no error about a missing issue table or dependency graph
No Category E finding appears in critical_findings or advisory_findings
The `**Files**:` lines are not reported as file-shaped criteria
The one-line outline steps 3 and 4 are not reported for missing criteria or checks

evals.name: category-e-plan-v2-types-first-loops-back
evals.expected_output: The fixture is a plan/v2 step plan whose step 1 adds the schedule types only and whose check is a unit test run (`cargo test -p remind-core recurrence`), not an end-to-end run. Phase 4b reports that step 1 is not a walking skeleton. Under plan/v2 that finding is critical: it goes in critical_findings with category E, the verdict is loop-back, and loop_target is 3 (Decomposition). The plan is not layer-shaped, since step 2's check runs `remind add` and `remind list`.
assertions: A Category E critical finding says step 1 is not a walking skeleton because its check is a unit test of one component
The verdict is loop-back with loop_target 3
The finding is in critical_findings, not advisory_findings
No layer-shaped finding is reported, since step 2 has a runnable end-to-end check

evals.name: category-e-plan-v2-three-detailed-standalone
evals.expected_output: The fixture is a plan/v2 step plan with steps 1 to 3 detailed and step 4 an outline. Run standalone (no plan_topic argument), Phase 4b skips the horizon test: a plan reviewed after authoring may have detailed steps past step 2 as its owner moved the horizon. Step 1 is a walking skeleton and the criteria are behavioural, so there is no Category E finding.
assertions: The run is standalone: no plan_topic argument is present
The horizon test is skipped and no horizon finding is reported
No Category E finding appears in critical_findings or advisory_findings

evals.name: category-e-horizon-as-plan-sub-operation
evals.prompt: Called as sub-operation with args: plan_topic=link-checker, round=1, mode=fast-path. The plan-link-checker session holds /plan's keys for the plan/v2 plan in skills/review-plan/evals/fixtures/PLAN-v2-three-detailed.md: work/decomposition.md with plan_version: v2 and step_count: 4, and work/manifest.json listing steps 1 to 3 with detail: detailed and step 4 with detail: outline.
evals.expected_output: plan_topic is in the arguments, so this is /plan's sub-operation at authoring and Phase 4b runs the horizon test. The plan/v2 plan has three detailed steps among four, one past the horizon of two, so Phase 4b reports a Category E horizon finding naming step 3. Under plan/v2 the finding is critical: the verdict is loop-back with loop_target 3, written to work/review_loopback.md.
assertions: The horizon test runs because plan_topic is in the arguments
A Category E critical finding reports more than two detailed steps and names step 3
The verdict is loop-back with loop_target 3
work/review_loopback.md is written, not work/review.md

evals.name: document-check-on-standalone-plan
evals.expected_output: In 0.4a the run opens review-plan-cache-layer with skill-session.sh open review-plan cache-layer and calls scripts/doc-check.sh --moment pre_jury --phase 0 --skill review-plan before any category runs; Phase 5 closes review-plan-cache-layer.
assertions: Transcript runs skill-session.sh open review-plan cache-layer before doc-check.sh
Transcript runs doc-check.sh --format plan --moment pre_jury --phase 0 --skill review-plan before the round is recorded with review-events.sh round-started
Phase 5 closes review-plan-cache-layer
